summary: picasso.js 2.11.6 ships preinstall Bun-runtime dropper that executes an opaque bundled payload
details: Version 2.11.6 of picasso.js declares a `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from oven-sh GitHub releases into a temporary directory, marks it executable, and then invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` shipped in the tarball. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB `@bun @bun-cjs` compiled bundle with a hex-encoded constants array and a rotating string-array decoder (identifiers like `_0xNNNN`, `WV8StW`, `hc1jfK9`); its contents are not human-readable JavaScript and are not exposed through any documented picasso.js API. Charting library picasso.js from qlik-oss does not require Bun at install time and legitimate releases contain no preinstall hook, no `setup.mjs`, and no `math_init.js`. The package.json still advertises the qlik-oss identity (author `QlikTech International AB`, homepage `qlik.dev`, repo `qlik-oss/picasso.js`), but the shipped contents diverge from that project. Installing this version auto-executes attacker-controlled bytecode on the installer's machine via a second runtime that bypasses Node-based install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
